title: Makar Chudra
author: Maxim Gorky
publication_note: first published in the newspaper «Kavkaz», Tiflis, 1892 (Gorky's first printed story)
source_note: Text from ru.wikisource.org, after M. Gorky's Complete Works.

art_alt.1_campfire: Old Makar Chudra with a long pipe by a campfire on the autumn steppe, a young traveller wrapped in a coat lying near, the camp and horses behind, the sea on the right
art_alt.1b_road: A winding road across the steppe to the sea at sunset, a traveller with a bag walking along it, a lone ploughman far away, wild geese in the sky
art_alt.1c_camp_nonka: The Gypsy camp at night with two covered wagons and a tent, proud Nonka in a red dress standing by a small fire, horses by a rail
art_alt.2_loiko_horse: Loiko Zobar galloping away on a white horse under the moon while soldiers guarding the stable sleep around a lantern
art_alt.2b_magnate: Radda in a green dress kicking a purse of gold into the mud, an old magnate on a pale horse looking on, a Gypsy wagon behind
art_alt.3_rider: Loiko Zobar riding out of the dark into the firelight with a fiddle in his hand, the camp sitting round the fire watching him
art_alt.3b_fiddler: Loiko Zobar playing the fiddle alone on a hill in front of a huge full moon, small campfires with listeners on either side below
art_alt.4_song: Loiko singing with his fiddle by the fire, Radda lying on her back looking at the stars, the elders sitting near, wagons behind
art_alt.4b_whip: Loiko thrown flat on his back, Radda smiling with a whip in her hand, the old men watching by the fire
art_alt.5_ravine: A moonlit ravine with a stream, Loiko sitting on a stone, old Makar lying on the bank watching, Radda coming from the distant camp fire

art_alt.6_circle: The camp gathered round the fire at dusk, Loiko with lowered eyes, Radda in green pointing to her feet

art_alt.6c_end: A dying fire in the rain, horses standing round in a ring, Makar wrapped in his coat asleep and the young traveller awake

glossary: a long, loose coat of coarse cloth worn by men of the steppe and the Caucasus.
Makar's pet name for the young man he is talking to.
the word Gorky uses; the people are today called the Roma.
a travelling company of Gypsy families with their wagons and horses (Russian: tabor).
the Hungarian leader of the 1848 revolution; Danilo says he fought at his side.
regions of the old Austro-Hungarian lands where the camp wanders.
a rich nobleman of Hungary or Moravia.
an old Russian weight, about 16 kilograms.
the mountain people of the Balkans, known for fierce pride and old customs.
summary: On an autumn night by the sea an old Gypsy tells a young traveller a legend: the proud beauty Radda, the free horse-thief and fiddler Loiko Zobar, and a love that could not bow. Gorky's first story, 1892.
site_description: Beside a campfire on the Black Sea steppe, old Makar Chudra tells a young wanderer about freedom, and about Loiko Zobar, a horse thief who played the fiddle like no one alive, and Radda, the proud Gypsy girl who loved her freedom more than the man she loved. Maxim Gorky's first published story (1892), in a full-cast English audiobook.

ru.description: Осенней ночью у моря старый цыган Макар Чудра рассказывает молодому страннику быль о красавице Радде и вольном конокраде и скрипаче Лойко Зобаре, о любви, которая не умела гнуть шею. Первый рассказ Максима Горького, 1892 год.
